featured_reviews.name: Jannat Sorathia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited this place on a recommendation with my cousin’s kids and honestly it turned out to be such a fun and memorable experience. The moment you enter you’re welcomed by different animal structures and statues, the entire space is beautifully designed with a jungle theme. Every corner looks vibrant and thoughtfully created, making it perfect for kids who love animals.

What really stood out to me was the mix of fun and learning. They have interactive setups like a bank counter, kitchen area, shopping mall and even a doctor’s clinic, which makes it engaging for kids while also being educational. There are plenty of activities to keep them busy along with cute rides and play areas.

The highlight has to be the crazy maze castle, it’s honestly something you need to experience to understand how exciting it is. I genuinely felt like I wish I was a kid again to enjoy it fully, even adults can have a great time here watching and being part of the fun.

Another thing I really appreciated is how many staff members are always around. They are very attentive and make sure the kids are safe and enjoying at all times. Even if you’re busy or just want to relax for a bit, you can trust them to take good care of your kids. It definitely feels like a very safe and well-managed environment.

They also have a very cute café serving pure vegetarian food. We tried pizza, pasta, fries, boba drinks and coffee, everything was quite good and perfect after all the activities.

I also got to know that the place can be booked for kids’ birthday parties and celebrations, which honestly makes it even more special.

Overall it’s truly a unique experience and definitely one of Mumbai’s first jungle adventure themed parks. I would highly recommend this place to anyone with kids, it’s something they’re going to absolutely love

featured_reviews.name: Amit Agrawal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Escapeverse and chose the "Murder on Eclipse Express" room. Based on the marketing and hype around their use of advanced technology and sensors, I had high expectations. Unfortunately, the experience did not justify the price we paid.

While the room does use a few sensors and automated mechanisms to unlock doors, the technology itself is quite limited and does not significantly enhance the gameplay. The "latest technology" claim feels exaggerated compared to what is actually offered inside the room.

The biggest disappointment was the storyline. As a murder mystery-themed escape room, I expected a logical and engaging investigation. Instead, many of the conclusions required players to make unrealistic assumptions, and the story progression often felt disconnected from the clues provided. Rather than rewarding logical thinking, several puzzles seemed to rely on guesswork. A good escape room should make players feel like detectives solving a mystery, but that feeling was largely missing here.

The room theme was "Murder on Eclipse Express," yet there was very little that made us feel like we were actually on a train. The ambience, setup, and overall immersion did not effectively support the theme. The train environment felt underdeveloped, which made it harder to connect with the story.

Another point worth mentioning is the room size. The space is quite limited and is best suited for 2–3 participants. Larger groups may find it cramped, with some members having little to do during certain parts of the game.

The overall condition of the premises was also disappointing. If you visit, I would recommend using the lift instead of the stairs, as the staircase were dirty and lighting was not there during our visit. Additionally, there were ants outside the room entrance, and some even got into my shoes, causing discomfort after leaving from venue. Basic cleanliness and hygiene around the venue should be maintained more carefully though inside cleanliness was good.

Finally, I was surprised by the handling of the payment receipt. After making payment, I requested a receipt but was initially told it could not be provided. It was only shared the following day via WhatsApp. A receipt should ideally be issued immediately upon payment.

Overall, I found Escapeverse to be significantly overhyped. The technology, storyline, immersion, venue maintenance, and customer service did not meet expectations for the amount charged. There is definitely room for improvement, particularly in creating a more logical story, enhancing the thematic experience, maintaining better hygiene, and providing a smoother customer experience.

We tried the Basement room and it was genuinely very scary, with great jump scares and a really immersive atmosphere that kept us on edge the whole time. featured_reviews.name: Deepika Pote
featured_reviews.review_text:
There are moments in life when your mind feels trapped in an endless loop of thoughts… when problems don’t just stay outside, they follow you everywhere. That’s exactly where we were... when we decided to try the Kohinoor room at Mystery Room, Andheri West..
and honestly, we didn’t realize then how much we needed it.
From the moment we entered, the energy shifted. The staff welcomed us with such warmth..always smiling, patient, and genuinely excited for us. It didn’t feel like just another activity; it felt like someone quietly telling us, “You’re going to feel better here.”
And then the game began.
What I loved the most was how brilliantly the clues were designed...hilarious, clever, and surprisingly nostalgic.. It was a reminder ...It felt like everything I had ever studied, observed, or casually learned in life was suddenly coming together. Each puzzle wasn’t just a task...it was a spark. A distraction. A reminder that the mind can still play, think, and solve… even when it feels heavy.
There were moments we laughed uncontrollably...cant tell you d exact details , moments we got stuck, and moments where we just looked at each other and said, “Wait… could it be this?” And when things started clicking, it wasn’t just about solving the room...it felt like breaking through something inside us. We dint panic ,got angry, or blamed each other but were focused on problem solving..
And then… that bell rang.
That sound ..it wasn’t just a signal that we had completed the task in hand... It was a jolt.... The exact jolt we didn’t know we needed... For those few minutes, we weren’t thinking about stress, worries, or anything weighing us down. We were just present, quick..and connected... We dint think ... We just did what needed to be done ..and laughed out our hearts....
We walked out lighter. Clearer. Almost reset.
If you’re feeling stuck, overwhelmed, or just mentally exhausted, this place is more than just an escape room. It’s a pause. A shift. A small but powerful break from the chaos inside your head.
For me and my sister, it wasn’t just an experience...it was a moment of healing.
A must-visit. Truly one of the best experiences we’ve ever had.

The ultimate test of wits and teamwork: "The Kon of Kohinoor" at Mystery Rooms Andheri. My team and I took on this "Mission Impossible" with just one hour on the clock, and it was a total blast. The room was packed with intricate puzzles and clever clues that kept us on our toes every single second. It felt like we were in a real-life spy movie, racing against time to steal the diamond.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a great time at Mystery Rooms Andheri. We played two games — Abduction and Night in Bhangarh, and both offered very different but equally exciting experiences.

Abduction was more of a pure mind game, focused on solving puzzles and thinking logically as a team — really engaging and satisfying.

Night in Bhangarh was the highlight for all of us — slightly spooky with dark horror themes, adding an extra thrill. The experience of crawling through spaces, solving clues, and escaping under pressure made it super immersive and fun.

Overall, a perfect mix of challenge, teamwork, and thrill. Great place to visit with friends if you enjoy puzzle-solving and a bit of adventure 👍

featured_reviews.name: mustafa ali
featured_reviews.review_text:
I wish there was an option to give negative ratings. I’ve been visiting this place quite often, around three times a month, with my two kids aged 6 and 3. On 21st December 2025, we visited again as it was a holiday. We booked a play session for both kids that included fries, juice, and a tattoo. The cost was ₹500 per child, which is higher than usual, but we agreed considering the inclusions.

Unfortunately, during playtime, my younger child had an accident and urinated in his jeans, which may have slightly wet the trampoline. This was completely unexpected, as he normally doesn’t do this. We were immediately informed by the receptionist and went to check. His clothes were wet, which we acknowledged.

What shocked us was the response from the staff. One staff member said, “Your child has peed on the trampoline, so it’s your responsibility to mop it.” This was extremely surprising and inappropriate. In kids’ play areas, it is generally expected that there is cleaning staff to handle such situations.

Although I was still willing to cooperate, another elderly staff member started arguing and rudely told my wife, “Aap bache ko diaper pehnana tha, hum saaf nahi karenge, aapko hi karna padega.” She literally shouted at her. This behavior was completely unacceptable and humiliating.

We explained calmly that most kids’ play zones have staff trained to manage such situations, but they insisted that their cleaner had already left and we had to clean it ourselves. The tone and attitude were extremely unprofessional. Eventually, after some discussion, we cleaned it ourselves just to avoid further conflict.

I strongly advise other parents to be cautious. This was a very unpleasant experience, and I don’t plan to visit this place again.

Additionally, they sell juices above MRP, which is illegal. I will be reporting this to the consumer forum so appropriate action can be taken. Hopefully, they will correct their pricing practices soon.

Overall, Zoobee Doobee is small, overpriced, and poorly managed. I genuinely hope Korum Mall introduces a better kids’ play area like Xperia at Lodha or Phoenix Marketcity.

featured_reviews.name: Shoaa Shams
featured_reviews.review_text: I had an absolutely thrilling time at Zero Latency Mumbai! Played Outbreak: Zombie for 30 minutes and the experience was next level. The free-roam VR, realistic weapons, and spine-chilling zombie attacks made it feel like I was living inside a movie. Super immersive, adrenaline-pumping, and a must-try for anyone who loves gaming and thrill. The staff was very polite, the environment was friendly i just wish the Zero Latency team could work on pricing. Its a little bit on the expensice side. But the overall experience is worth it!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thanks so much Shoaa we are thrilled with your review .

featured_reviews.review_text: Amazing experience, went today with my son and we had the place to ourselves. Played Far Cry VR. The staff are really helpful and everything is as immersive as you’d expect. Will go again. Thanks to the team for making it so good.
